subject: Subprocessor rotation: PayMo analytics -> Streamlight (evidence request)
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@paymo.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: paymo-legal@paymo.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: Streamlight replacing TelemetryOne as analytics subprocessor (effective 2025-07-15)

Hi Laura,

Quick heads up from PayMo's ops team — we're rotating our analytics subprocessor for event-level telemetry (used for product analytics and billing signals) from TelemetryOne to Streamlight, target cutover 2025-07-15.

Summary: Streamlight will ingest anonymized event streams (no raw PII in the payload), provide pre-aggregations for dashboards, and host the intermediate metrics store in us-west-2. They use AWS KMS (us-west-2) and forward aggregated traces to our DataLake in us-east-1.

Attached: paymo-subprocessor-notice-20250630.pdf (signed notice), plus Streamlight's SOC2 summary (pdf) and a preliminary dataflow diagram (png).

Ask for Redwood: can you confirm whether this change requires an amended DPA annex or a short evidence package? If so, what minimal artifacts you need and whether we should route this via procurement/legal.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call.

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Technical Ops, PayMo
liam.oconnor@paymo.com

Subject: Re: Notice: Streamlight replacing TelemetryOne as analytics subprocessor (effective 2025-07-15)

Liam —

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the initial artifacts. A couple quick clarifying questions from our side:

- Confirm scope: you said "anonymized event streams" — will Streamlight see any stable user identifiers (customer_id, account_id) in the ingestion pipeline, or are those hashed/removed prior to handoff?
- KMS/Key jurisdiction: is the KMS in us-west-2 owned/managed by Streamlight, or by PayMo? We need the key ownership and region for our export and encryption mapping.
- Retention + export: how long do they retain raw events (if they do ingest them), and what retention applies to aggregated metrics?
- Onshore fallback: if Streamlight needs to route traffic for certain customers, are there contractual constraints for EU/UK customers?

Ben / Naomi — looping you in for technical and compliance review. Can you confirm the minimal evidence package we should ask PayMo/Streamlight for so procurement/legal doesn't need to push a DPA amendment? My inclination: if Streamlight never processes raw un-anonymized PII and KMS is PayMo-managed, then a short evidence bundle (SOC2 summary, dataflow diagram, KMS attestation, and scope statement) should suffice. If keys are Streamlight-managed or they store raw IDs, we escalate to DPA annexing.

Marissa — FYI in case legal/procurement should coordinate a brief addendum.

Laura Bennett
Senior Privacy Manager | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 10:11:44 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: Streamlight replacing TelemetryOne as analytics subprocessor (effective 2025-07-15)

Laura / team —

Quick technical read:
- If Streamlight only receives hashed or ephemeral ids and does not persist raw PII, risk is low. We should confirm hashing algorithm (one-way salted hash) and whether PayMo does client-side hashing before egress.
- KMS: if Streamlight manages the key, we need key rotation policy and whether they allow BYOK (bring-your-own-key). That impacts cross-account exportability and legal hold capabilities.
- Requesting: Streamlight SOC2 summary (they attached), encryption attestation (who holds keys), retention matrix (raw vs aggregated), and network egress regions.

If they provide the four artifacts above and confirm no stable PII, allow process to continue as a notice + evidence. Escalate to DPA annex only if any of those are not met.

Ben
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Sophie Renaud <sophie.renaud@streamlight.io>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@paymo.com>
Cc: paymo-legal@paymo.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: Streamlight replacing TelemetryOne as analytics subprocessor (effective 2025-07-15)

Hi Laura / Ben —

Thanks for the quick review. Attached: streamlight-soc2-summary.pdf and streamlight-dataflow-diagram.png. Answers inline:

- Stable IDs: Streamlight receives only event-level payloads with account_id (GUID) which PayMo hashes client-side with a per-tenant salt prior to egress. We do not accept raw email addresses or un-hashed PII.
- KMS: PayMo will provision a customer-managed KMS key in us-west-2 and we will use that key for server-side encryption at rest. We support BYOK and can provide a KMS attestation screenshot for the key ARN.
- Retention: raw event buffer retained for up to 72 hours for ingestion smoothing, aggregated metrics retained 25 months by default (configurable).
- EU/UK routing: Streamlight has a eu-west-1 cluster but for PayMo EU tenants we recommend onshore routing; we will include routing controls in the onboarding checklist.

Also sharing a link to an onboarding DocuSign with a short SLA appendix and a checklist: https://www.docusign.com/embedded?env=prod&doc=PAYMO-STREAMLIGHT-SLA

Let us know the one-pager you'd like for procurement/legal and we can produce a tailored attestation.

Best,
Sophie
Partner Integrations | Streamlight

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Renaud <sophie.renaud@streamlight.io>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@paymo.com>

Subject: Re: Notice: Streamlight replacing TelemetryOne as analytics subprocessor (effective 2025-07-15)

Thanks Sophie — that addresses the key items I asked for.

Next steps for Redwood:
1) Please upload a one-page KMS attestation (ARN + confirmation PayMo provisioned key) and a brief retention matrix (we can accept a table image or short PDF).
2) PayMo please confirm which customer tenants (list or hubspot ids) will be affected by the 7/15 cutover so we can mark them in our controls registry.
3) Marissa/legal: if procurement is happy with Streamlight's BYOK and attestation, we will process this as a Notice + Evidence and append a short subprocessor addendum (no full DPA change). If procurement requests, Marissa, please flag by EOD Fri.

If we get those artifacts by EOD Thu (7/3), privacy/compliance can sign off for a 7/15 cutover for non-EU tenants; EU routing will require confirmation of eu-west-1 routing controls.

Laura
Senior Privacy Manager | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachments referenced above: paymo-subprocessor-notice-20250630.pdf (notice), streamlight-soc2-summary.pdf (attestation), streamlight-dataflow-diagram.png (diagram).
